6\text{ shrimp/minute}\times 10\text{ minutes}=60\text{ shrimp}.

shrimp.
Here's another detail: Emily peels and sautes each shrimp sequentially rather than simultaneously.

Since Emily works on each shrimp sequentially:

- Peeling time: \(\frac{1}{6}\) minute per shrimp.
- Sautéing time: \(\frac{10}{30}=\frac{1}{3}\) minute per shrimp.

Thus, each shrimp that is peeled and sautéed takes

\[
\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{1}{2}\text{ minute}.
\]

In 10 minutes, she can process

\[
\frac{10}{1/2}=20\text{ shrimp}.
\]

\[
20-5=\boxed{15}
\]

shrimp that she can successfully sauté.

- Peeling time:

\[
\frac{95}{6}\text{ minutes}
\]

- Cooking time for 90 shrimp:

\[
\frac{90}{3}=30\text{ minutes}
\]

Total time:

\[
\frac{95}{6}+30=\frac{275}{6}=45\frac{5}{6}\text{ minutes}.
\]

Thus, it will take Emily

\[
\boxed{45\text{ minutes }50\text{ seconds}}
\]

to peel and cook 90 usable shrimp.
